result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_edges_as_tuples()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Return list of edges as (id, source, target) tuples. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3335-L3369){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_edges_as_tuples() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns all edges in the graph as tuples containing the edge ID and the source and target node IDs. Useful for iterating over all edges or analyzing edge structure. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of tuples where each tuple is (edge_id, source_id, target_id). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Get all edges in a graph: ::: {#8717c099 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) # Iteration over edges - each tuple is (edge_id, source, target) for edge_id, source, target in graph.get_edges_as_tuples(): pass # Process each edge ``` :::
